extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, federal science administrators, National Academy of Sciences, state education officials, and program designers for national scientific training/selection
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for organizing a national scientific research foundation and for discovering, selecting, and training scientific talent (including veterans and youth). Covers administrative structure, selection committees, tests/rating instruments, and educational/policy recommendations to expand and balance scientific training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording in-service training for credit (USAFI No. 47)
rubrics_metrics.description: Service in-school training should be recorded on the official form USAFI No. 47 and returned by the man or woman in the armed forces to the secondary school for evaluation and the award of credit toward graduation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This will facilitate a continuance of education in college of qualified persons. Veterans of World War II who do not file a USAFI credit application form before leaving the service should use a certified copy of their separation record as evidence of in-service training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use certified separation record if USAFI form not filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Veterans who do not file a USAFI credit application form before leaving the service should use a certified copy of their separation record as evidence of in-service training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an alternative documentary procedure to ensure veterans can obtain secondary-school credit for in-service training and thus continue education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of handling scientific/technological talent in armed forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate handling of the education of the scientific and technological talent now under arms is a primary test of the Government's effectiveness in meeting the overall problem addressed by the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The future scientific and technical leaders are largely in military service; unless exceptional steps are taken to recruit and train talent from the armed service at or before the close of the war, the country's future scientific leadership will be seriously handicapped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build talent-discovery plans on existing educational structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A plan for discovering and developing scientific talent in American youth must be built upon the country's existing educational structure and be consonant with its current operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a plan must recognize the limited number of high-ability individuals and ensure that the relatively few with creative capacity in science are found early and helped and encouraged to continue through the years required for professional and research training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early identification and long-term support of able students
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure relatively few individuals with creative capacity in science are found early and are helped and encouraged to go on through the years of study required to complete professional and research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To enlarge the small group of exceptionally able men and women, it is necessary to increase the number of able students who go to college — this involves early schooling, better high schools, and measures that help promising students persist to college and graduate study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide educational programs suited to diverse students
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational programs should be provided that are suited to different students so that they do not become bored and drop out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide suitably differentiated programs is cited as a cause of premature leaving from high school; designing varied curricula and opportunities is essential to retain capable students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active recruitment by business and industry to retain promising youth
rubrics_metrics.description: Active recruitment by business and industry of promising youth should be balanced with encouragement for those youth to continue their education for both individual and national interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business and industry recruitment can draw promising students away from continued education; policies should encourage industry to support continuation rather than premature labor-force entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assist needy high school students to prevent forced withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide provision for assisting needy students in high school who must take jobs to help support themselves or their families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic need is a significant reason for students not continuing to college; local communities and states should provide support so capable students are not lost for financial reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary responsibility lies with local, business, and State governments
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsibility for improving conditions that cause able students to be lost to higher education is primarily upon the local community and business interests and the State governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, it must be recognized that some sections of the country lack resources to provide adequate high schools; federal or national plans should be designed with that in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase college-going able students via better high schools and opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: To increase the number of able students who go to college requires more and better high schools, with provisions for helping capable students in the high schools and opportunities for promising high school students to go to college.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any failure to provide these opportunities constitutes indefensible and wasteful utilization of higher education and neglect of human resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider labor-market demand when enlarging graduate training
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for enlarging the number of students entering graduate schools to be trained for research must be considered in relation to the probable demand for trained research workers as expressed in available jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While necessary to enlarge graduate numbers to produce research students of exceptional ability, the danger of an over-supply of trained research personnel must be kept constantly in mind (avoid repeating the European postwar surplus mistake).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance recruitment across scientific and non-scientific fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for recruiting more college students into the physical and biological sciences and enlisting more graduate students for training in research should be viewed in the light of the overall needs of the country and of the requirements in other fields of research and the professions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If too many high-quality students are absorbed by fields of scientific research, research in the social sciences and in the arts and humanities may be jeopardized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a National Scientific Research Foundation to administer programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose establishment of a foundation charged with responsibility for the administration of the several national scientific programs being recommended; such a foundation should have power to make contracts with other agencies for performance of functions within its scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation (or similar agency) is recommended to make arrangements for choosing Scholars and Fellows through the National Academy of Sciences, giving the program respect and prestige.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use National Academy of Sciences to sponsor scholar/fellow selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation, or any similar agency, should make arrangements for choosing Scholars and Fellows under the proposed plans through the National Academy of Sciences, if that organization be willing to accept the responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Association with the National Academy, as representative body of scientists, would lend respect and prestige to the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint National Science Reserve Advisory Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the National Academy of Sciences, with the advice and consent of the Administrative Committee of the National Research Council, should periodically appoint a National Science Reserve Advisory Committee to advise regarding methods of selection and arrangements for the entire program within legislative provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory committee provides periodic oversight and method guidance for selection and program arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint a full-time Director to run the National Science Reserve Program
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the National Academy, with advice of the advisory committee, should appoint a Director of the National Science Reserve Program who would devote his full time to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to general supervision of the Administrative Committee, the Director would establish a national office, select administrative and research staff, develop detailed plans and administer the program; the Director would also appoint technical advisory committees to develop tests of scientific promise, the inventory of activities and interests, and the recommendation blank and rating scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop tests, inventories, recommendation blanks and rating scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical advisory committee(s) appointed by the Director should develop tests of scientific promise, an inventory of activities and interests, and the recommendation blank and rating scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These instruments are required for systematic selection of Scholars and Fellows; the Director and technical committees are responsible for development and standardization.

rubrics_metrics.name: State selection committees composition
rubrics_metrics.description: State committees of selection should be appointed to consist of five members: three scientists, one of whom should serve as chairman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a specific structural requirement for decentralized selection panels to ensure scientific representation and leadership at the state level.
